title: Integral finite-Tor-amplitude complexes form a triangulated subcategory
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and a scheme $Y$; put $A_{E,j}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^j$ for $j\geq1$. Let $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)\subset D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ be the derived-complete bounded constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], a triangulated subcategory [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated], and for $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ let $K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,j}\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,j})$ be its derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. Let $P$ be the property of $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$: $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, and there are integers $a\leq b$ such that $K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,j}$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] for every $j\geq1$. Then $P$ is closed under isomorphisms and defines a full triangulated subcategory of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]: $0$ satisfies $P$; $K$ satisfies $P$ if and only if $K[m]$ does, for every $m\in\mathbf Z$; and for every distinguished triangle $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ with $K$ and $M$ satisfying $P$, also $L$ satisfies $P$.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 21.46.4 (Tag 08G2, label lemma-cone-tor-amplitude), part (2), applied to the reductions, which carry distinguished triangles of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ to distinguished triangles of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,j})$ and commute with shifts; the integral category follows the blueprint node def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude (literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-smooth-purity/sk-def-sf-operations/def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude.md)
